judgment: The mandatory criterion is observable native editing and actual saved-byte preservation with the required normal quit/new-process reopen evidence on the frozen package. It is not a requirement that every historical failed automation run acquire a proven cause before a later strict positive case can satisfy that criterion.

Current retained positive cases meet those observable criteria without product changes, relaxed content oracles, repeated input or replacement of the original negative proof. Waiting for actual readiness and taking read-only snapshots do not weaken the save-result criterion.

The old failed attempt is valid negative evidence and cannot be called harmless or falsely green. Missing receiver/handler and immediate pre-save context prevents proving that the same ready-save action failed in the product. The new common barrier prevents proving a QA fix or a timing cause.

Accordingly there is no identified missing mandatory save case to execute again merely to explain the old failure. Its causal investigation is a separate unresolved observation, not an invented new release gate.

uncertaintyAndDisclosure.classification: Failure occurred during automated native operation; causal QA-versus-product classification is OPEN, not a proven harmless QA failure or confirmed/repaired product bug.
uncertaintyAndDisclosure.releaseRiskText: In one earlier automated Mac Suite save preflight, an edit was visible and dirty but the requested CmdS did not update the private test file. Six later fresh-copy controls and the regular same-package native save/reopen cases succeeded. The original cause is unknown; an intermittent product-save problem is not excluded by these results. Original failed proof and forced cleanup remain preserved.

necessaryNextAction: No new build/test loop is required by this remaining item under the fixed bounded criteria.
